subject: Private deployment: license scope & alternatives to source escrow
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@biomedhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Biomed Health Legal <legal@biomedhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify on-prem license scope and escrow alternatives

Connor — thanks for the demo last week. Legal reviewed the MSA + Order Form and we have two primary asks before procurement can sign: 

1) License scope: the current language in §2.1 reads as a hosted-service license. For our on-prem (airgapped) deployment we need explicit language allowing "operation and maintenance" by our SOC team and the option to run the runtime inside our VPC without Redwood operator access. Can you confirm the exact license grant you intend for private deployments (including whether runtime binaries/containers are covered)?

2) Escrow-like assurance: because we are in regulated workflows, our compliance team wants a mechanism to ensure continuity if Redwood cannot support an on-prem deployment (e.g., insolvency, acquisition). We are open to alternatives but need technical proof points. Examples we considered: 
  - Source code escrow (hard ask)
  - Signed, notarized snapshot of runtime + model weights (we know weights may be restricted)
  - Operational playbook + witness test / on-site acceptance procedure

Can Redwood legal propose a pragmatic alternative to full source escrow that meets auditors? If you can send a short position + any proposed addenda language, that would help our counsel.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement aims to finalize on Friday.

Best,
Anna Lopez
Head of Procurement
Biomed Health
[Attachment: BH_MSA_comments_20270419.pdf]
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@biomedhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem license scope and escrow alternatives

Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. We can absolutely work through this. Quick answers up front, then I’ll loop in Legal/Engineering for proposed wording: 

• License scope: Redwood's standard private-deploy offering grants a "non-exclusive, non-transferable license to operate and maintain the Redwood Inference runtime and related artifacts for the customer's internal processing within the agreed deployment boundary." That covers runtime containers and compiled binaries we deliver for the private deployment; it does not include source code unless specifically negotiated. 

• Escrow alternatives: we generally avoid full source escrow. Reasonable, commonly accepted alternatives we can offer: 
  1) Staged forensic snapshot: signed and encrypted runtime artifact + activation manifest deposited with a neutral custodian (access staged upon predetermined triggers and joint witness test).
  2) Operator runbook + reproducible witness test: detailed runbook + a one-time witnessed transfer test with customer's engineers to validate deployment/run.
  3) Signed attestation + 90-day remediation SLA with optional transfer of operational artifacts (subject to export/IP constraints).

I'll ask Marissa (legal lead on privdeploy) and Karthik (ops/infra) to draft short redline language and an addendum that tracks an "escrow-lite" path so you can take to counsel. Would you prefer a custodial deposit (third-party escrow agent) or an on-prem witnessed-test-only approach? Both are workable but differ on lead time and cost.

Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify on-prem license scope and escrow alternatives — proposed positions and redline plan

Forwarding Anna's ask with a proposed approach we should take to Legal. Key points for internal alignment before we prepare a redline: 

Summary of constraints (ops/legal):
- We can grant operation and maintenance rights to the customer for delivered runtime containers and compiled artifacts. Cannot include unpublished source or proprietary model weights unless separately negotiated and compensated.
- Custodial escrow of models is typically a non-starter (IP/external distribution & licensing constraints).

Proposed "Escrow-lite" package (tiered options to offer):
A) Witnessed Transfer + Runbook (preferred low-friction path)
   - Deliver: immutable runtime artifact (signed container images), deployment runbook, KMS integration doc, and access test plan.
   - Action: one witnessed transfer day (on-site or secure remote with screen+log capture) where Redwood and Biomed complete a go-live checklist.
   - Trigger: customer can initiate re-run of transfer in event of Redwood insolvency or failure to remediate within SLA window.

B) Custodial Snapshot with Staged Access (higher assurance, higher cost)
   - Deliver: signed, encrypted snapshot of runtime artifact + activation manifest deposited with neutral custodian (we propose IronVault as an example).
   - Access: manifest unlocks only on documented, contractually defined triggers (insolvency, breach of contract where Redwood cannot reasonably cure).
   - Note: model weights remain excluded unless we have an explicit license and export clearance; if customer requires weights, billable negotiation required.

C) Operational Attestation & Extended SLA (compliance-focused)
   - Deliver: signed attestation of operational artifacts + 90/180-day remediation guarantees; optionally include transitional support credits.

Next steps for redline:
1) Draft short addendum text that 1) clarifies license grant for private deployments (explicitly list runtime containers, compiled artifacts, and operational rights); 2) enumerates the Escrow-lite options and the triggers/conditions for custodial access; 3) includes a runbook/witnessing exhibit and a short SLA clause.
2) Karthik to confirm technical feasibility for the signed container + runbook and provide the witness-test checklist.
3) I will prepare initial MSA redline and a single-page addendum summary to attach to our reply.

Attachments referenced for drafting: [Attachment: template_escrow_lite_exhibit.docx], [Attachment: witness_checklist_v1.xlsx]

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Platform & Privacy | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem license scope and escrow alternatives

Anna — attaching our proposed MSA redline and an addendum that lays out the "escrow-lite" options (witness transfer, custodial snapshot, and attestation + SLA). High-level: 

• License language: explicit grant to operate and maintain delivered runtime artifacts and compiled containers within the customer's deployment boundary. We added a short exhibit that lists what is included (container images, configuration artifacts, runbook) and what is excluded (source code, proprietary model weights unless separately licensed).

• Escrow-lite addendum: three-tier options described, with triggers and a neutral-custodian flow for Option B. We included a short witness-test checklist as an exhibit so auditors can see the play.

• Logistics: if Biomed prefers the witnessed-transfer path, propose a joint working day (remote or on-site) within 30 days of go-live to perform the transfer. If Biomed prefers custodial snapshot, we will need a statement of fees and choose a custodian; that typically adds 6–8 weeks to delivery.

Please find attached: MSA_Biomed_redline_v1.docx and PrivDeploy_Addendum_v0.3.pdf (summaries + exhibits). If your counsel is comfortable, we can incorporate edits and aim to finalize the addendum by end of next week. Would you like to schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk counsel through the witness checklist?
